title: Section 8 Landlords in Lakewood: Dense Doubles, ZIP 44107 and the Registration Rule
metaTitle: Section 8 Landlord in Lakewood OH: What's Different
metaDescription: Section 8 landlord Lakewood Ohio guide: the registration CMHA collects with your RFTA, ZIP 44107 payment standards, and what a two-family unit changes.
secondaryKeywords: renting to voucher tenants lakewood ohio
answerBox: Lakewood is one of 17 suburbs where CMHA must collect a Certificate of Occupancy and/or Rental Registration with your RFTA packet, and it ties your first HAP payment to that occupancy permit. In ZIP 44107, CMHA's FY2026 two-bedroom payment standard is $1,536 — a hair above the $1,525 county median.

sections.h2: The paper you hand over with the RFTA
body: CMHA names the city outright. Its Leasing with CMHA page requires a copy of the **Certificate of Occupancy and/or Rental Registration** with the Request for Tenancy Approval for units in **17 named suburbs** — Lakewood among them, alongside Euclid, Fairview Park, Parma, Shaker Heights and twelve others.

Read the mechanism, not just the list. This is not CMHA vetting you: it states that **"CMHA does not have a pre-approval process for landlords or units."** The gate is municipal; CMHA enforces it at the RFTA window. For City of Cleveland units CMHA verifies registrations itself through the City's Citizen Access Portal, effective October 1, 2025 — see [Renting to Voucher Tenants in the City of Cleveland](/section-8-landlords-cleveland-ohio/). In Lakewood the document is yours to produce.

It is also a condition of getting paid: on a new contract **"you will be paid on the next scheduled payment date after HCVP has received three copies of the signed contracts, the executed lease and occupancy permit, when applicable."** Lakewood's fees and renewal cadence are not numbers we will invent — they differ by municipality, and CMHA's advice is to ask the building department before you sign a lease.

sections.h2: ZIP 44107 pays a median number, not a premium one
body: CMHA sets payment standards **per ZIP code** under Small Area Fair Market Rents — HUD lists it as a mandatory SAFMR agency — publishing FY2026 figures effective **January 1, 2026** for 53 ZIP codes. Lakewood addresses sit in ZIP 44107. ZIP boundaries and city lines do not coincide, so look your address up in CMHA's Rent Determination tool: there is no static PDF, and the table shown before you pick a ZIP is a placeholder.

items: 44107 is a **median ZIP**, not a high one: its studio standard equals the countywide median, its two-bedroom sits $11 above it, and the top tier pays **$2,169** on the same two-bedroom

Against the nearest Cleveland ZIPs the gap is real — **$1,536 in 44107 against $1,276 in 44102 and $1,333 in 44111**. Countywide the two-bedroom runs $1,096 to $2,169, so any standard quoted without a ZIP is meaningless: see [CMHA Payment Standards by ZIP Code](/cmha-payment-standards-by-zip-code/)

The standard is not a ceiling on your rent. CMHA: **"The payment standard is NOT the maximum amount that the landlord can charge; it is the maximum amount of subsidy that the CMHA will pay toward each tenant's rent portion"**

sections.h2: So does a Lakewood rent clear?
body: Three rules decide that, and none is the payment standard. **Rent reasonableness** comes first: under 24 CFR 982.507(b) the comparison weighs location, quality, size, unit type and age, plus amenities and utilities, against comparable unassisted units; a unit that is not rent reasonable is ineligible. Second, CMHA applies that test to **gross rent** — rent plus tenant-paid utilities or the utility allowance — so who pays the gas in a shared-basement double moves the number. Third, the tenant's portion on an initial contract can be **no more than 40% of the family's monthly income**; above that CMHA negotiates the rent down. Where an asking rent runs well above the 44107 standard, that gap does not quietly land on the tenant — it can stop the deal, and side deals to cover it are prohibited.

Much of Lakewood's rental stock is halves of two-family houses and suites in small apartment buildings, which the program handles differently from a single-family house ([more for 1-4 unit owners](/section-8-for-small-landlords-1-4-units-cleveland/)).

Bedroom count is the first trap. If a family picks a unit larger than the bedroom size on its voucher, CMHA applies the payment standard **and** utility allowance for the smaller of the two: a three-bedroom up-and-down leased to a two-bedroom voucher is priced at $1,536 in 44107, not $1,977. Check the voucher's size and its expiration, **180 days from the issue date**, before taking the unit off the market.

Utilities are structural here. CMHA's January 1, 2026 allowance schedule carries separate lines for a single-family dwelling, for **"Townhouse, Duplex/Triplex, Row House"** and for a multi-unit apartment, so building type is part of the pricing decision. Two suites are also two tenancies — the rule that a family **"may not submit... more than one (1) RTA at a time"** limits the family, not you, so both halves mean two packets, two inspections and two 60-day HAP execution deadlines.

Shared systems concentrate the risk. CMHA's 24-hour emergency list fails a unit on the spot for items including a missing or inoperable smoke or carbon monoxide detector, **no heat between October 15 and April 15**, a gas leak, or unlockable windows within six feet of ground level. Since **December 29, 2024** smoke detectors must sit on each level, in each sleeping area, within 21 feet of each bedroom door and in any living area separated by a door, sealed 10-year or hardwired. If one boiler serves both halves of a double, a heat failure is not a one-unit problem — and **"[r]ent is abated when the unit fails to pass on two consecutive inspections."**

sections.h2: Is it worth doing in Lakewood?
body: The tenant pool is large — CMHA markets **"over 15,000 voucher holders"** — but none of it is compulsory here. The U.S. Commission on Civil Rights' Ohio Advisory Committee states that **"Source-of-income discrimination is legal in most of Ohio,"** and PRRAC's March 2026 compilation names five Cuyahoga County municipalities with source-of-income bans: Cleveland Heights, University Heights, South Euclid, Warrensville Heights and Linndale. Lakewood is not among them, so this is a business decision rather than an obligation.

Weigh it against what CMHA does not stand behind. Its owner pitch promises **"[s]table, guaranteed rent payments deposited directly into your account"** — CMHA's word, not ours — while it states flatly that **"HCVP does not pay for tenant caused damages."** Screening remains the landlord's responsibility, exactly as with any other tenant.

sections.h2: How we work a Lakewood unit
body: We work Greater Cleveland and Cuyahoga County under CMHA, and **we have completed CMHA's Virtual Landlord Orientation** — mandatory since January 1, 2026, required every 24 months of the owner or managing agent, and verified before CMHA can execute a HAP contract on a new tenancy. With us as agent, that step is already done.

items: **Tenant placement — one month's rent**, charged only after the tenant is placed. No placement, no fee
**Inspection attendance with a written report — $100.** Attend yourself instead and pay nothing
**Ongoing management — 5% of monthly rent**, only while the unit is rented
**Repair estimates — free, itemized, back within 24 hours.** Nothing starts without your approval

body: Lakewood adds one municipal document to the RFTA and one condition to your first payment run, and pays a county-median ceiling in ZIP 44107. The deal turns on bedroom count, gross rent and the 40% test. Call **(440) 444-4737** or read [Section 8 Stress Free](/section8stressfree).

faq.q: Do I need a rental registration to rent to a voucher tenant in Lakewood?
faq.a: CMHA requires a copy of the Certificate of Occupancy and/or Rental Registration with the RFTA packet for units in 17 named suburbs, and Lakewood is one of them. It is a municipal requirement CMHA enforces at the RFTA stage, not a CMHA approval.

faq.q: What is CMHA's payment standard in Lakewood?
faq.a: CMHA sets standards by ZIP code. In ZIP 44107 the FY2026 standards effective January 1, 2026 are $1,118 studio, $1,276 one-bedroom, $1,536 two-bedroom, $1,977 three-bedroom and $2,113 four-bedroom — the two-bedroom sitting $11 above the $1,525 countywide median. Confirm your exact address in CMHA's Rent Determination tool.

faq.q: Lakewood rents run high. Can I still charge market rent on a voucher unit?
faq.a: The payment standard caps the subsidy, not your rent — CMHA says so explicitly. What limits the number is rent reasonableness under 24 CFR 982.507(b), applied to gross rent including tenant-paid utilities, plus the 40%-of-monthly-income ceiling on the tenant's initial portion.

faq.q: My applicant wants the three-bedroom suite but holds a two-bedroom voucher.
faq.a: CMHA applies the payment standard and utility allowance for the smaller of the voucher size and the actual unit size. In ZIP 44107 that prices the tenancy at the $1,536 two-bedroom standard rather than $1,977, so check the voucher before taking the unit off the market.
